- When sentiment is positive (≥ 0.33) and forecast is below recent high, adjust upward by 1–2% to capture bullish momentum.  
- When sentiment is negative (≤ -0.25) and forecast is above recent low, adjust downward by 1–2% to reflect bearish pressure.  
- Avoid over-optimistic forecasts after sharp price spikes; reduce peak predictions by 5–10% to account for mean reversion.  
- If 3+ consecutive forecast days show upward trend but true outcome is flat or declining, reduce forecast slope by 15–25% to avoid over-leverage.  
- For 30-day horizon, if true outcome exceeds forecast by >5% for 3+ days, apply a “lag correction” — reduce next forecast by 2–5% to avoid overestimating future momentum.  
- If sentiment history shows no clear trend (all 0.00), use 30-day moving average of past 18 days as baseline, then adjust ±1% based on volatility of last 3 days.
